Rock Etam
rok EE-tam
proper noun
Hebrew Sela' 'Etam, “the rock of Etam,” 'Etam meaning “place of ravenous creatures” or “lair,” and sela', a cleft rock or crag; Samson’s stronghold in Judah.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

After Samson smote the Philistines hip and thigh with a great slaughter, “he went down and dwelt in the top of the rock Etam” (Jdg 15:8), the cleft crag whither the enemy dared not follow. Thither three thousand men of Judah went down to fetch him, fearful of their masters (Jdg 15:11), and bound their own deliverer to hand him over. The rock was Samson’s refuge, a high stronghold in the day of his strength; yet the deliverer of Israel was himself a flawed and divided man, and the rock could shelter his body but not mend his soul. Here the type strains toward its fulfilment. Samson hid in a rock, but he was not the Rock; he saved with one hand and fell by his own lusts with the other. He points beyond himself to a greater Deliverer, the spiritual Rock that followed Israel, and that Rock was Christ (1Co 10:4), a hiding place from the wind, a covert from the tempest, the shadow of a great rock in a weary land (Isa 32:2). In Him the people are hid indeed, not for a season but for ever, and He needs no cleft to shelter Him, for He is the cleft in which we shelter. Rock Etam teaches us to flee from every flawed savior to the true Rock of ages, cleft for us, in whose wounds the church finds a refuge that no Philistine and no death can storm.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The cleft rock where Samson dwelt after smiting the Philistines, whence Judah fetched him (Jdg 15:8, 11); a figure of the cleft rock of refuge and of the true Rock, Christ.

expand to see more

ROCK ETAM, the cleft crag where Samson dwelt (Jdg 15:8).

Thither he went down after smiting the Philistines hip and thigh.

Three thousand men of Judah came to fetch him from the rock (Jdg 15:11).

The rock sheltered his body, but could not mend his soul.

A figure pointing beyond a flawed deliverer to the true Rock, Christ.

📖 Key Scripture

Jdg 15:8 — "And he smote them hip and thigh with a great slaughter: and he went down and dwelt in the top of the rock Etam."

Jdg 15:11 — "Then three thousand men of Judah went to the top of the rock Etam, and said to Samson, Knowest thou not that the Philistines are rulers over us? what is this that thou hast done unto us? And he said unto them, As they did unto me, so have I done unto them."

1Co 10:4 — "And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ."

Isa 32:2 — "And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Rock Etam recovers the cleft rock as refuge, and the flawed deliverer of Israel pointing beyond himself to the true Rock of ages.

expand to see more

Rock Etam was Samson’s stronghold, a cleft crag whither the Philistines dared not follow; yet the deliverer who hid there was himself a flawed and divided man, saving with one hand and falling by his lusts with the other. The rock could shelter his body but not mend his soul, and so it strains toward a greater Deliverer.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A cleft rock in Judah raises no modern quarrel. The principle to recover is that every flawed savior points beyond himself to the true Rock, the spiritual Rock that followed Israel, which was Christ. He is the hiding place from the wind, the shadow of a great rock in a weary land; flee from every lesser refuge to the Rock of ages, cleft for us.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From sela', a cleft rock or crag, and 'Etam, “lair” or “place of ravenous creatures.”

expand to see more

Sela' 'Etam — the rock of Etam (Jdg 15:8).

sela' — a cliff, crag, or cleft rock.

'Etam — perhaps “lair” or “place of birds of prey.”

A stronghold in the territory of Judah.

The cleft where Samson hid from the Philistines.

Usage

"Samson went down and dwelt in the top of the rock Etam."

"Men of Judah fetched Samson from the rock Etam."

"The rock Etam was a cleft stronghold in Judah."
